$description: Everything a designer might tune in the 3D scenes: quality tiers, the studio light that metal reflects, and each scene's size, detail per tier, scroll keyframes and budget. Colours are token paths into packages/tokens (for example color.brass.200 or scene.light-key); finishes come from material.* tokens. Shapes that follow content (pentagon faces, syllabus tiles) take their count from the content, not from here. See docs/design/scenes.md.

tiers.$description: full: high-end devices. lite: four cores or fewer, or 4 GB of memory or less. still: reduced motion, Save-Data or no WebGL2, which get a still image instead.

studio.$description: Glowing panels the metal reflects (an environment map), and a few direct lights. Ported from the v3.2 scene, with colours from tokens.

medal.$description: The struck brass medal: the official medal image on the face, its normal map for relief, a reeded edge and two rims.

reedLevels.$description: Bump heights of the edge ridges, 0 to 1: groove, then ridge.

float.$description: The medal bobs gently while on screen: height in world units, and the time for one bob.

pointer.$description: The medal leans towards the pointer: the largest lean in radians, and how much of the gap it closes each frame.

still.$description: The progress shown as a still image on the still tier.

kota-prism.$description: The Kota pentagon: a prism with one engraved plate per point of the Kota system (packages/content/blocks/{locale}/kota-system.json). Scrolling turns each plate to the front in turn.

plate.$description: Texture width in pixels; its height follows the face's proportions. Sizes are fractions of the width; labelTop is a fraction of the height.

fit.$description: On narrow screens the camera moves back until this much of the prism's radius fits across, so no plate is cut off.

assemble.$description: The plates fly in before the prism turns (as in v3.2). until: the share of the section's scroll the assembly takes; the turning plays over the rest, and the page's list of points follows from there. distance and lift: how far out and up or down a plate starts (world units); spin and tumble: how much it is turned as it starts (radians); stagger: how much later each plate starts than the one before (share of the assembly).

syllabus-slab.$description: The opening scene of the syllabus page: the chapter tiles set into a stone slab with a brass edge, and the JEE Advanced only chapters as detached rows below (docs/design/syllabus-table.md).

camera.$description: From a low angle over Physics to straight above, framing the whole slab at any screen shape; fit is the share of the screen the slab fills.

specimens.$description: One object per subject in a glass case on a brass base: a pendulum (Physics), a benzene molecule (Chemistry) and a surface plot (Mathematics).
